new_theme: Modify L1 (dev): add a rectangular-pulse matched filter to an NRZ test pattern. The start graph is a Vector Source of 24 +-1 symbols at 8 samples per symbol (32 kHz) -> Throttle -> File Sink nrz.dat. The task asks for a new File Sink mf.dat (float) that holds, for every input sample, the average of that sample and the 7 before it. There is one output per input sample with no extra delay, each value must be within 0.001, and nrz.dat must stay unchanged. The reference adds a Moving Average (length 8, scale 1/8). v2 cells: the start is data_source (train), which does not matter for a modify start; the reference and every variant are data_source|filter -> dev. cluster_id: chain:data_source|filter. compose.audit_items finds no other item in this cell.
deviation_from_plan: The brief proposed f2p equal_prefix on mf.dat if Moving Average and FIR [1/8]*8 are bit-identical, and otherwise corr_ref >= 0.9999 plus max_abs. Moving Average and FIR are exact. But an FFT filter, which the brief's graph check accepts, is correct and is not bit-identical, so exact equality would reject a valid answer. corr_ref + max_abs alone would not pin the stated 0.001 tolerance. So the oracle combines four checks: signed corr_ref with no lag >= 0.99999 over samples 7-390, rms within 0.1 % over the same window, max_int_dev with scale 8 <= 0.008 (tooling T3), and min/max = -1/+1 within 0.001 over the whole capture. Together they imply that every value in the corr window is within 0.001 of the ideal; the derivation is in the build.py docstring. The variant v2 (FFT filter) passes. The first 7 outputs are excluded: there, 'the 7 samples before it' do not exist. Two of the brief's mutants cannot be written as single-edit mutants of the reference: the decimating integrate-and-dump and a filter fed from a delayed branch. They are probes instead (integrate_and_dump, fir_one_sample_late), and both fail as expected.
